$comment: Provenance for the third-party skills vendored into .claude/skills/ (ADR-0201).
Pinned by commit, not by branch: a skill that changes under us changes how every
session behaves, so an update is a reviewed commit like any other.
`skills` is an allowlist of UPSTREAM directory names — curation is the point, so a
skill that is not listed is not taken. `excluded` records what was refused and why;
a sync reports any upstream skill in neither list, so a --bump surfaces new
candidates instead of silently adopting or silently dropping them.
Run `node .claude/vendor/sync-skills.mjs` to re-materialise exactly this state.

excluded.git-workflow-and-versioning: Prescribes trunk-based development, its own branch naming, and a semver/changelog release flow. This repo decided branch-per-task and Conventional Commits, and has no versioning scheme.
excluded.documentation-and-adrs: Ships its own ADR template and threshold. Ours is decided and stricter — root CLAUDE.md's 'write only what a future reader would otherwise get wrong', and amend in place.
excluded.using-agent-skills: A meta-router whose decision tree points at the three skills above; with them gone it routes to absent skills.

rewrites.why: Its TDD skill is renamed to clear the collision with superpowers'; the sibling skills that route to it by name have to follow.
git-workflow-and-versioning is excluded; commit guidance here is the repo's own.

excluded.using-superpowers: Demands a skill be invoked 'before ANY response including clarifying questions' and that the model 'does not have a choice'. That is the opposite of this repo's context-engineering rule — load the minimum for the change in front of you.
excluded.using-git-worktrees: Sets up worktree isolation as a precondition. Our sessions are already isolated by branch-per-task, and `.claude/worktrees/` is gitignored scratch.
excluded.finishing-a-development-branch: Offers 'merge back to <base> locally' as an option. Root CLAUDE.md forbids committing onto local main, and a finished task ends in a pull request.

rewrites.find:
name: design-taste-frontend
description: Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. The agent reads the brief, infers the right design direction, and ships interfaces that do not look templated. Real design systems when applicable, audit-first on redesigns, strict pre-flight check.
rewrites.replace:
name: taste-skill
description: Anti-slop frontend critique (tasteskill). Use as a second opinion when a Travelive surface or mockup looks generic, templated or AI-made - weak hierarchy, uniform spacing, card soup, gratuitous motion - and before calling a UI change visually done. In this repo it is a critic, not a designer - palette, type, color roles, RTL and the component library are fixed by docs/design/design-language.md and the design-mockups skill, and those win every disagreement; never install a design system or font it recommends. Upstream's own scope is landing pages and portfolios.

rewrites.why: The skill fetches its rules at run time from web-interface-guidelines@main, which would bypass the pin. Point it at a pinned commit; move this hash on a --bump like any other.
The description gains this repo's scope, so it is matched on a review and the rules that assume an English, hover-first page are read against ours.
rewrites.find: description: Review UI code for Web Interface Guidelines compliance. Use when asked to "review my UI", "check accessibility", "audit design", "review UX", or "check my site against best practices".
rewrites.replace: description: Review UI code for Web Interface Guidelines compliance (Vercel's accessibility, focus, forms, motion, typography and performance rules, fetched from a pinned commit). Use when asked to "review my UI", "check accessibility", "audit design", "review UX", or "check my site against best practices", and on any frontend/ or mockups/ change before calling it done. Where a rule assumes an English, desktop or hover-first page - curly quotes, hover-only feedback, LTR - root CLAUDE.md, design-language.md and the RTL rules win.

fetchedAtRuntime.$comment: Content a skill reads over the network instead of from the tree, each pinned by commit in the URL the skill fetches. A --bump does not move these: update the hash here and where it is used, together.
fetchedAtRuntime.https://github.com/vercel-labs/web-inter: e3d624baaf29dc1fc645aff3e38f03e564d2d6b1 — command.md, read by web-design-guidelines (rewrite above).
fetchedAtRuntime.https://github.com/VoltAgent/awesome-des: f6961238d5cddcf8042a74a70fc400ec67181abb — design-md/<brand>/DESIGN.md, read by our own awesome-design skill. 74 brand analyses, 2.9 MB; fetched per brand rather than vendored because a session needs one or two, not all.

sourcesRefused.$comment: Asked for, cloned, measured, and not taken. Recorded so the question is not reopened from memory — see ADR-0201.
sourcesRefused.https://github.com/nextlevelbuilder/ui-u: 7 skills, 69k+ lines, 11 MB — a palette, type scale and font/icon corpus (5.5 MB of TTFs, an 824 KB icon index) that exists to decide what a UI looks like. That is decided here by docs/design/design-language.md and ADR-0028, and drawn by the design-mockups skill.
sourcesRefused.https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable: 1 skill, 72k lines, 3.5 MB — mostly bundled browser JS for its own anti-pattern detector. The detector is the good part; without its 3 MB of scripts the skill is only a competing design language, and with them it is the single largest thing in the repo.
